brief: Goldman's Louis Miller argues AI hyperscaler credit spreads (GSUCHS30, GSXUHYPR) are at their widest levels of the year; the last time spreads were this wide, the underlying equities were 15% lower, implying either credit is wrong or hyperscaler stocks have another 15% to fall. Supporting evidence: hyperscaler CDS hit a record, seven of 20 junk-rated AI data center bonds depend solely on CoreWeave as tenant, and Goldman's AI beneficiaries basket is down 25% from its June high versus the S&P ex-AI. The capex debate has shifted from spending growth to financing and returns: hyperscaler capex growth peaked at 116% y/y in Q3 2026 and consensus sees it slowing to roughly 20% by end-2027, so its contribution to S&P EPS growth falls from +11pp in 2026 to +7pp in 2027 to -1pp in 2028 as depreciation bites. Broader market internals (elevated puts, high beta breaking down, growth pricing more pessimistic than GDPNow) corroborate caution, though NDX valuation at 21x is not stretched. Miller is not calling a crash; he expects rotation rather than index-level weakness, and recommends five trades: buy the S&P ex-AI broadening, Quality (with a stretched-RSI caveat), a midterm ACA healthcare bet, Brazil ahead of the October 25 runoff, and hedging/shorting Taiwan semis.
